registry_info.name: service_yard
registry_info.description: A synthesis artifact for the `upkeep` family (7 registry names, 5 scripts, 1 shared const carried by 3 of them). One piece of equipment parked sixteen times across four kerbed bays, so the four conditions of its working life stand in one frame.
registry_info.note: Per-token registry file so parallel builders never share one JSON. The `upkeep` word and its four values are PRELOADED from station_plinth.gd at runtime and validated in both directions at _ready; do not retype them here or in the script. This artifact does NOT declare upkeep as an axis — see dna.declines.

service_yard.name: Service Yard
service_yard.description: Four kerbed bays round a quad, lettered with the station kit's own four words — service, works, store, scrap — read out of station_plinth.gd's const at build time rather than retyped. The same pump skid is parked in every bay and dressed by that bay's condition: cover on and lamp lit in service; panel swung out, loom spilling and a trestle over it in works; sleeved and banded in store; cladding gone, core bared and taped in scrap. A fleet of sixteen units is distributed across the bays by one stationary solve, and the routes between the bays are laid in the aisles. `policy` is the yard's rule for a unit that falls due, which sets the whole picture through that one solve; `circuit` is how much of the passage between conditions is drawn. Nothing animates, nothing is grabbable, nothing is random: one four-state solve per build, read three ways.
interactions: walk the four bays and find the same skid in all four conditions
at loop, follow the barred plate: that arrow is the one route the yard never takes
at traffic, read the store bay's dwell column against the two posts feeding it
switch policy to cannibal and watch six of the sixteen units move into the scrap bay
service_yard.qfep_connection: A condition is a decision, not a property. The same machine is `service` or `scrap` according to a rule written somewhere else, and the four rules in this yard never touch the equipment — they only change what the yard does about it. The `traffic` rung is the artifact's own dark spot: the moment it stops showing four bays and starts showing two numbers about them, built so the two summaries of one solve visibly disagree. And the loop the brief asked for turns out to belong to the FLEET, not to the object: scrap is absorbing, the return leg is a purchase order, and the yard says so with a bar rather than a caption.
service_yard.relationships: Synthesised from the seven registry names that declare `upkeep` — station_wall, station_plinth, station_plinth_wide, station_pillar, station_micropod, station_floorline, station_crates — which resolve to five scripts. Replaces none of them and re-runs none of their axes from the outside.

spatial_needs.footprint_note: The apron is 6.50 m along X by 4.00 m along Z, so a 7 x 4 clear patch. The two near bays' name tabs stand on the +Z edge and the two far bays' on the -Z edge, facing outward, so the yard reads from either long side; `orientation: face_approach` plus a rotation in the map token is how you pick one. There is no collider anywhere in the file, so the pathfinder will route straight through the bays — correct, because there are no bays, there is a picture of a yard.
spatial_needs.shelf_rule: a space, not an object (base 6.86 m, h 1.00 m, registry.measurements)

measurements.measured_by: Computed from the script's own layout constants and re-derived in a Python replica of the geometry; no Godot was run, per the brief. MeshInstance3D only, which is what the capture AABB counts, and every drawn node in this artifact is a MeshInstance3D (BoxMesh, plus HangarKit.stencil / brand_patch quads). No MultiMeshInstance3D, no CSG, no particles, so no `layers = 0` anchor is needed and none is present. X is 6.86 and NOT the apron's 6.50: the four dwell columns at `traffic` stand outboard of their bays at x = +/-3.25 and their datum collars are 0.36 wide, reaching +/-3.43. Z is the apron's 4.00. Y runs from 0 (the apron underside, so the grid's base-to-floor grounding is a no-op and no auto_ground opt-out is needed) to 1.00 = the `works` trestle rail at 0.96 plus half its 0.08 section. The dwell ceiling is 1.20 m but the tallest column any policy actually reaches is 0.600 m at hoard/store, so it does not set the box.

dna.axis_shape: `policy` sits SIDE BY SIDE — four institutions with the same four conditions and four different rules about them, none contained in another, so they are a set and any two of them are a comparison. `circuit` NESTS — bays is contained in line is contained in loop is contained in traffic, each rung keeping every mark the last one drew and adding to it, so it is a ladder and must be swept in order. Declared parallel-first for law 15: dropping the tail of a parallel axis loses a case, dropping the tail of a nested one only lowers the ceiling. At the gallery's DEFAULT cap of 9 a 4x4 declaration renders 4x2, which keeps all four policies and trims circuit to [loop, bays] — the ladder's default and its floor, the most informative two-value truncation available. THE FULL SHEET NEEDS --max=16.
dna.default:
policy=repair, circuit=loop. A SYNTHESIS HAS NO SHIPPED PLACEMENTS, so there is nothing to preserve and the default is a free design choice; the rule that outranks everything in doc/DNA_PROMOTION_BRIEF.md governs promotions of placed artifacts and has no work to do here. That freedom was spent on the strongest single reading rather than the emptiest.

WHY `repair` AND NOT `cannibal`. The artifact's thesis is that a yard holds all four conditions at once, so a default that empties a bay would be contradicted by its own arithmetic. Every policy here occupies all four bays — that was a design constraint on the rates, checked before anything was built, and two earlier rate sets were thrown out for producing an empty scrap bay at repair and an empty works bay at hoard. `repair` is the most evenly spread of the four (7/4/2/3 of sixteen) and the only one where no single bay dominates the frame; `cannibal` (5/3/2/6) and `hoard` (6/1/8/1) are louder and each of them announces its answer before a visitor has read the four words. A visitor who meets only the default meets the question.

WHY `loop` AND NOT `bays`. `bays` is the emptiest rung by definition: four conditions and no claim about how anything gets between them, which is exactly the picture every one of the seven family members can already produce on its own. It is the control, not the exhibit. `loop` is the first rung where the yard's own claim is legible without a caption — six lit legs closing a circuit, and one barred plate standing across the one arrow the naive reading invites and the circuit never takes. `traffic` was considered and passed over for the reason slack_yard passed over `scored`: it is the strongest single frame and it hands the visitor two numbers before they have seen the topology those numbers are about.
dna.was: did not exist. Nothing was promoted here and no shipped behaviour was touched. This is the cross-member argument the seven `upkeep` declarations leave unbuilt: every member's own promotion block describes the four conditions as a lifecycle, and not one of them can stand two of them at once, because a body can only be one way at a time.
dna.kin:
THE WORD IS TAKEN WHOLE AND NEVER RETYPED. service_yard.gd opens with
const UPKEEP_SRC := preload("res://commons/artifacts/station/station_plinth.gd")
and the four bays, their names, their order and their count all come out of UPKEEP_SRC.UPKEEPS at build time — the bays ARE the family's array, not a copy of it. station_plinth.gd is the one read because it is the script three of the seven registry names resolve to (station_plinth, station_plinth_wide and station_micropod are one scene under three names, the corpus's most common hidden family), and because it is one of the three files carrying the const. _check_family_list() runs at _ready and push_errors in BOTH directions: a value the family declares that this yard has no bay builder for, and a builder this yard has that the family has dropped. It also errors if the family stops having exactly four values, because the quad layout is what makes every real leg an edge rather than a diagonal.

THE CONST IS BYTE-IDENTICAL IN THREE FILES, checked rather than assumed. station_floorline.gd:73, station_plinth.gd:90 and station_wall.gd:59 all carry
const UPKEEPS: PackedStringArray = ["service", "works", "store", "scrap"]
with the same md5 (0b63357ffaa4) on the whole line. station_pillar.gd and station_crates.gd have NO const — they read config_upkeep straight into the export with no validation at all, which is a second-order finding: a map token misspelling `upkeep: storr` is silently ignored by the plinth, the wall and the floorline and silently accepted as a no-op by the pillar and the crates.

THE MEANING OF THE WORDS, AND A DIVERGENCE ON THE RECORD. The brief that commissioned this yard glossed `works` as 'in operation' and `service` as 'opened up and being maintained'. The family's CODE says the opposite, in all five scripts: `service` is 'in commission — the legacy lineage, byte for byte' and `works` is 'mid-job — a trestle barrier standing ACROSS the run'. Both readings are natural English, which is why they drifted. This yard follows the code, because the code is what seven registry entries and their live placements mean. The brief's argument survives the swap intact: the state in which a thing is most itself and least useful is `works`, the one with its guts out.
dna.family_order:
TAKEN: service, works, store, scrap — the const's order, and the order 6 of the 7 registry entries declare.
THE OTHER: service, store, scrap, works — station_crates.json alone.

WHY THE OTHER EXISTS, which nobody had written down. station_crates.gd is one of the two scripts with no const. Its registry list is its own _build() BRANCH ORDER with the export default hoisted to the front: `if upkeep == "store"` at line 117, `if upkeep == "scrap"` at line 120, and the trailing `if upkeep == "works"` at line 161. It is derived from the code; it is just derived from a different part of the code than the other six.

WHY IT MATTERS, with the threshold. build_dna_gallery trims a value list from the TAIL. The six const-order entries end ...store, scrap; crates ends ...scrap, works. So at --max 3 the six are measured on {service, works, store} and crates on {service, store, scrap} — DIFFERENT SETS, not merely a different tile order — and at --max 2 it is {service, works} against {service, store}. The two orders agree only at the full 4. This is strictly worse than the `slack` family, whose three orders all agreed down to cap 3 because they shared a common tail. A single-axis `upkeep` sweep across this family must run --max=4 or it compares unlike with unlike, and any past sweep run below that should be re-read before its numbers are trusted.
dna.note:
THE ARGUMENT, AND WHY IT NEEDS A YARD RATHER THAN A MEMBER.

Every one of the seven family members can be caught in exactly one of the four conditions, because a body can only be shaped one way at a time. Each member's own promotion block describes the four as a working life — a lifecycle, a sequence, a set of moments — and not one of them can put two of those moments side by side. The yard parks the SAME piece of equipment sixteen times across four bays and varies the rule instead of the object.

LAW 2, DECIDED FROM THE MEMBERS' CODE RATHER THAN THEIR PROSE. The four values are MIXED, and the mixture is asymmetric:

  works NESTS ON service in 5 of 5 scripts. station_crates._build() runs the whole legacy stack loop and only at its last line calls _upkeep_works(); station_pillar and station_floorline both build the legacy body and append _upkeep_works() after the match. works = service + apparatus.

  store and scrap DO NOT NEST, and they are opposite operations. store ADDS A COVERING (pillar wraps a sleeve, floorline sheets a board runner over the strip) — nothing is removed from the graph and the lit surface is OCCLUDED. scrap SUBTRACTS MATERIAL (pillar swaps its shaft for _scrap_shaft()'s stripped frame; floorline rebuilds the lit run as dead metal). station_crates makes it explicit: both values `return` before the legacy loop ever runs.

So there is one containment inside a set of four conditions of which no member contains all the others — the PARALLEL case, which is exactly the condition under which showing them all at once is NOT merely the top value. The yard therefore stands all four simultaneously, exhibits the word, and sweeps something else.

ONE COPY OF THE ARITHMETIC (law 3), READ THREE WAYS. _solve() runs a four-state stationary solve once per build — power iteration, a FIXED 4000 steps, no tolerance and no early exit, so it does the same float arithmetic in the same order every time. Its result is read as (1) how many units stand in each bay, largest-remainder rounded from pi * 16; (2) how much moves along each leg, pi[from] * P[from][to], drawn as a post; (3) how long a unit dwells in a bay, pi itself, drawn as a column. It is never re-solved.

WHAT IT FOUND, all computed in Python before anything was built:

  policy    pi_service  pi_works  pi_store  pi_scrap   units in each bay (of 16)
  repair       0.4644    0.2167    0.1382    0.1806    7 / 4 / 2 / 3
  replace      0.4075    0.1902    0.2303    0.1721    6 / 3 / 4 / 3
  cannibal     0.3332    0.1555    0.1381    0.3732    5 / 3 / 2 / 6
  hoard        0.3446    0.0846    0.5003    0.0705    6 / 1 / 8 / 1

  leg flow      due      fix     down    issue     cond     repl
  repair     0.1300   0.1192   0.0279   0.0387   0.0108   0.0108
  replace    0.1141   0.0418   0.0245   0.0967   0.0723   0.0723
  cannibal   0.0933   0.0746   0.0200   0.0387   0.0187   0.0187
  hoard      0.0482   0.0440   0.0758   0.0800   0.0042   0.0042

THREE THINGS IN THOSE TABLES ARE THE ARTIFACT.

(1) THE LOOP BELONGS TO THE FLEET, NOT TO THE OBJECT, and this contradicts the brief that asked for the yard. The brief says the life of a piece of equipment 'is not a line but a loop'. For the OBJECT that is false: scrap is absorbing. A condemned unit does not come back. The scrap -> store leg is not the same skid returning; it is a REPLACEMENT being bought, which is why its rate is called `repl` and why it is the only leg in the yard that is not a movement of the thing it is drawn next to. The loop closes through PROCUREMENT. What loops is the fleet; what runs in a line and stops is the unit. The yard's own claim is therefore narrower and truer than the one it was commissioned to make.

(2) THE NAIVE READING IS ONE THIRD RIGHT, AND THE GEOMETRY SAYS SO WITHOUT A CAPTION. The `line` rung walks the family's array pairwise and draws the three arrows a value list invites. service -> works is REAL (it is the `due` leg). store -> scrap is BACKWARDS — that edge exists and carries `repl`, in the other direction. works -> store is FICTIONAL: the circuit never joins that pair, so that arrow is the only DIAGONAL in the artifact, cutting across the middle of the yard where every other mark runs down an aisle. At `loop` the barred plate is placed on whichever consecutive pair of the family's array has no real leg behind it — asked, not told, so reordering UPKEEPS moves the bar by itself.

(3) DWELL AND FLOW DISAGREE, which is the whole justification for the `traffic` rung. At `hoard` the store bay carries the tallest dwell column in the sweep (0.600 m) and the two legs feeding it carry the shortest posts in the sweep (0.017 m). A bay can be full because things arrive fast or because they never leave, and a still cannot tell you which unless it shows you both numbers off the same solve. At `repair` the ranking inverts: the service bay's column is 0.557 m on a `due` post of 0.520 m, the busiest leg in the whole sweep.

THE RATES ARE THE POLICY, NOT THE OUTCOME. It would have been easy to pick a target allocation and back out rates that produce it; that is engineering the number. The six rates per policy were chosen from each rule's meaning first (a cannibal yard buys nothing, so `repl` is 0.05; a hoarding yard rarely issues, so `issue` is 0.16) and the allocations are whatever those rates imply. Two earlier rate sets were discarded for a stated reason: the first produced an empty scrap bay at `repair` and the second an empty works bay at `hoard`, and a yard whose thesis is that all four conditions are present at once cannot have its default contradict itself.
dna.measured: PREDICTION NEARLY RIGHT, AND RIGHT ABOUT THE SHAPE. Swept 2026-08-13, sixteen frames. It said the closest pair is `circuit` bays against line AND THAT IT IS A CLUSTER OF FOUR RATHER THAN A SINGLE PAIR. bays-against-line is the weakest circuit pair at three of the four policies (0.61% cannibal, 0.64% repair, 0.64% replace) and the cluster claim holds; the overall minimum, 0.48%, lands one step away at policy = hoard on line against loop. `policy` is the healthy axis at 1.55-4.57%, weakest at cannibal against repair in every circuit — which is honest, since cannibalising and repairing are the same yard activity differing in where the parts go. Left alone.
dna.predicted_degeneracy:
PREDICTED BEFORE ANY CAPTURE, in the critic's own currency rather than in changed pixels, because a prediction in the wrong units is a prediction about a different instrument. The critic crops to the union of the two frames' subject boxes, neutralises each frame's own background, converts to greyscale, RESIZES TO 160 x 160 and takes the mean of the hottest 5%. The numbers below come from rasterising this exact geometry at this exact camera (FOV 34, PAD 1.9, yaw 0.62, pitch -0.26, 760 x 760, dna.framing 0.62) in Python with a z-buffer and a fixed key light, then pushing the result through that same pipeline.

THE CLOSEST PAIR IS circuit `bays` <-> `line`, AND IT IS A CLUSTER OF FOUR, NOT A SINGLE PAIR. Measured at all four policies: cannibal 3.55%, repair 3.74%, hoard 3.82%, replace 3.94%. Those are the four thinnest pairs in the whole sweep and the fifth thinnest is `loop` <-> `line` at hoard, at 7.94% — more than twice the gap. The clustering is part of the claim: bays -> line adds exactly the same three arrows, six gate posts and three chevrons at every policy, and nothing else in the pair of frames differs, so the four numbers should sit within about half a point of each other. If they spread by more than a point, the sweep is not holding the policy fixed across the circuit rung.

AXIS MEANS over the 24 same-axis pairs each: policy focus 26.68% (min 15.75, max 36.99); circuit focus 18.29% (min 3.55, max 31.13). Both should read BITES.

IT WILL BE FLAGGED AS A TWIN, AND THE FLAG IS CORRECT. 3.55% clears the critic's INERT bar of 3.0% but sits well under its TWIN_FOCUS bar of 6.0%, so the pair will be re-measured per channel — and unlike slack_yard's `gauged`/`scored` pair, THE PER-CHANNEL RE-MEASURE WILL NOT RESCUE IT. Every mark `line` adds is worn metal at body_color darkened 0.26 to 0.36; there is no accent, no emissive and no hazard stripe anywhere in the naive reading, precisely because the naive reading is the one the yard disagrees with. It should land in the critic's TWINS list, not in its COLOUR-ONLY list. If it lands in colour-only, something has tinted the naive marks that should not have.

WHY IT IS THIN, said in numbers so it is not read as a fault. `line` adds three 0.30 m lanes (2.60 + 3.13 + 2.60 = 8.33 m of lane, 2.50 m2 of ground), six 0.08 x 0.52 m posts and three 0.36 x 0.26 m chevrons, to a yard that already carries sixteen dressed units, four pads, four kerb sets and four lettered tabs. The ground marks foreshorten by sin(15 deg) = 0.26 at this camera, so 2.50 m2 of paint projects as about 0.65 m2. This is the field_room ruling applied in advance: the pair is thin because the thing it describes is a small addition, and it is left alone rather than engineered up to clear a bar.

A PREDICTION THAT ALREADY PAID FOR ITSELF, BEFORE THE CAPTURE. The first replica of this geometry measured that same cluster at 5.32-5.83%, not 3.42-3.94%. The 1.5x discrepancy was not noise: the first cut of _build_naive() branched on along_x / along_z and built the works -> store DIAGONAL as an AXIS-ALIGNED BOX spanning its own bounding rectangle — a 2.72 x 1.55 m grey slab through the middle of the yard, 4.5x the ink of the 0.30 x 3.13 m lane it was supposed to be, and nothing like an arrow. Predicted-against-predicted caught it; nothing else in the chain would have, because a big grey slab in the middle of a yard is exactly what a diagonal route looks like if you never rasterise it. It is now one yawed lane with no special cases.

AND ONE PAIR PREDICTED **NOT** TO BE DEGENERATE, because it looks like it should be. `repair` and `replace` differ by only two unit-moves out of sixteen (7/4/2/3 against 6/3/4/3) and are the obvious candidate for a policy twin at the three rungs where the routes carry no numbers. They are not twins and measure 22.8-25.1% at bays / line / loop, because a unit is a 0.56 x 0.55 m dressed object at 45 x 44 px and moving two of them between bays also swaps their DRESSING — a service unit becomes a store unit, cover-and-lamp becomes sleeve-and-straps. If that pair does come back as the tightest policy pair, the units are photographing as undifferentiated boxes and the condition dressing is not reading, which would be a real finding and the opposite of this one.

WHAT WOULD FALSIFY THIS.
(a) If the closest pair comes back as `loop` <-> `line` instead, the replica overstated how much the standing guide rails survive the 160 x 160 downsample — they are 0.09 m thick, 7.3 screen px, under two samples, and they are carried in the prediction by their 105-210 px length rather than their thickness.
(b) If `policy` comes back under about 12% focus, the sweep is not reaching the axis: check that `fleet` has not been overridden to a value that makes two allocations collide.
(c) If ANY pair reads 0.00%, run tools/check_dna_declarations.py --token=service_yard first — a value the code cannot reach falls back to the default and prints identical tiles.
dna.framing_why:
DERIVED FROM THE UNION AABB ACROSS ALL SIXTEEN FRAMES, not from the default. Union 6.86 x 1.00 x 4.00 (x across the two bay columns, z across the two bay rows); diagonal sqrt(47.0596 + 1.0 + 16.0) = 8.0037, radius 4.0019. The rig is dist = radius / tan(FOV/2) x PAD x framing with FOV 34 and PAD 1.9, so framing 1.0 puts the camera at 4.0019 / 0.305731 x 1.9 = 24.8747 m and shows a 15.207 m frame around a 6.86 m object — PAD 1.9 already shows 1.9x the bounding-sphere radius, which is why a wide flat object wants framing well below 1.0.

AT 0.62 the camera comes to 15.4194 m and the frame to 9.4284 m, which is 80.61 px per metre. Rasterised at that setting the subject's bounding box spans 80.1% of frame width and 29.6% of height, with 71 px of clear margin on the tight side, and the subject covers 11.1-11.8% of the frame depending on the variant — well above the ~6% dilution floor. 0.60 was measured too (82.6% of width, 61 px on the tight side, 83.29 px/m) and rejected: 61 px is thinner than this artifact needs, because the showcase key light's specular fringe is not modelled in the replica and the outermost marks here are the dwell columns, which exist only at one rung.

WHY THE UNION AND NOT THE DEFAULT: the apron is 6.50 m wide but the four dwell columns at `traffic` stand OUTBOARD of their bays and reach x = +/-3.43, so the union is 6.86. Framing off the default (`circuit=loop`, which has no columns) would have seated the camera 2.6% closer and pushed the outer columns toward the edge in the four frames that have them. Everything else in the artifact is the full 6.50 x 4.00 at every value of both axes — apron, pads, kerbs, tabs and all thirty-two slot positions are drawn identically in all sixteen frames — so the box does not move between tiles for any other reason.

LAW 10 CHECK, BECAUSE 11.5% SUBJECT LOOKS LOW. It is not a small subject, it is a SPARSE one, and the box is full in width: 80.1% of frame width against 29.6% of height. A yard is mostly apron. taxonomy_hall reports 10.4% for the same reason and is correctly framed; the test is whether the union box is full or airy, and this one is airy by design because the empty ground between four bays is what makes them four bays.

GAUGE CHECK AT 80.61 px/m, because foresight_range shipped 0.028 m arrows onto an 18 m lane. The critic downsamples its crop 3.81x (609 px of subject box to 160), so a mark must clear about 15 screen px to survive as four samples.
  MARKS THAT ENTER A PAIR DIFF, and must clear the bench:
    unit body        0.50 x 0.42 m -> 40.3 x 33.9 px    (policy moves these between bays)
    store sleeve     0.62 x 0.54 m -> 50.0 x 43.5 px
    works trestle    0.82 x 0.94 m -> 66.1 x 75.8 px
    naive chevron    0.36 x 0.26 m -> 29.0 x 21.0 px    (the bays -> line delta)
    gate post        0.08 x 0.52 m ->  6.4 x 41.9 px
    arrowhead plate  0.28 x 0.22 m -> 22.6 x 17.7 px    (the line -> loop delta)
    guide rail       0.09 m thick  ->  7.3 px thick, 105-210 px long
    flow post        0.60 x 0.14 m -> 48.4 x 11.3 px, up to 41.9 px tall
    dwell column     0.26 m wide   -> 21.0 px, up to 48.4 px tall
  MARKS THAT DO NOT, and are gauged for a human at 760 px instead:
    lamp block       0.10 x 0.07 m ->  8.1 x  5.6 px
    name tab         0.62 x 0.18 m -> 50.0 x 14.5 px
    datum collar     0.05 m tall   ->  4.0 px tall, 56 px long
  The second group is legitimately below the bench bar because none of it ever enters a pair difference: the tabs, the collars and the lamps are drawn identically in all sixteen frames. The lamp distinguishes one BAY from another WITHIN a frame, which is the exhibited family word, not a swept axis. Saying which marks are for the bench and which are for the visitor is the point of running this check at all.

THE VERTICAL MARKS ARE VERTICAL ON PURPOSE, and it was measured. The first cut drew the whole circuit flat — painted lanes and ribs, no rails, no plates — and the replica measured circuit at 12.91% mean with a floor of 1.77%, under the critic's INERT bar. The camera pitches only 15 degrees down, so a floor mark projects at sin(15) = 0.259 of its length and a standing one at cos(15) = 0.966, a factor of 3.7. Adding standing guide rails and arrowhead plates without changing a single route took the same axis to 18.29% mean with a floor of 3.55%. That is a fact about the standpoint, not about the routes, and it is the reason the flow gauge is a POST rather than a lane width.
dna.fixture_note:
NO FIXTURE AND NO SEED IS NEEDED, and it is checkable rather than claimed. The file contains no randf, no randi, no randomize, no _process, no _physics_process, no Timer, no Tween, no physics body and no reference to the scene tree outside its own children and its own ancestors' metadata. _ready is ungated: it reads config metadata, validates the family list and builds the whole yard standalone, so the sweep's rescue path (call apply_grid_config when the AABB measures zero) will never fire.

THE SOLVE IS DETERMINISTIC BY CONSTRUCTION, which is the one place this artifact could have leaked non-determinism. _solve() power-iterates for a FIXED 4000 steps with no tolerance, no early exit and no convergence test, so it does the same float arithmetic in the same order every time. The largest-remainder allocation breaks ties by bay index, not by iteration order, so it is a pure function of pi. Two captures of one value are two photographs of one object.

THREE WAYS IN, ONE DOOR. The sweep sets the @export directly before add_child; the grid stamps config_policy / config_circuit metadata, which _meta_str walks up to four ancestors for before _ready builds; and apply_grid_config takes a dictionary. All three are validated against the POLICIES and CIRCUITS lists, and apply_grid_config rebuilds ONLY when a value actually changed AND _ready has already built once — the force_pad fault. An unrecognised word keeps the standing value rather than silently building a default.

BOTH AXES ARE @export_enum STRING ENUMS, not bools, so the fixture-string trap (a typed bool rejecting the string "true" before _ready) cannot occur here. Both hints are on ONE line each, so the declaration gate's line parser can see them.

ONE LATENT FAULT FOUND ON AUDIT AND MADE LOUD RATHER THAN FIXED AWAY. `fleet` is map-overridable and _read_config_meta clamps it to 4..32, where 32 is the yard's TOTAL slot capacity (4 bays x 8 slots). That bound is only reachable if the allocation were even, and it never is. Measured across all four policies: at the shipped fleet of 16 the worst case is hoard/store at EXACTLY 8 of 8 — zero headroom — and at fleet 17 that bay is allocated 9, so the ninth unit is never drawn while its dwell column still reports pi = 0.5003. At fleet 32 the yard would silently drop 5 to 11 units depending on policy. A frame showing eight units beside a gauge reporting nine is a disagreement no still can expose, which is exactly the class of fault law 6 names. _build_bay now push_errors when a bay is allocated more units than it has slots. The default is untouched: no bay overflows at fleet 16 under any policy, so no capture changes. The clamp was deliberately NOT tightened to a safe constant, because the safe bound is policy-dependent (17 for hoard, 20 for repair, 24 for cannibal) and a single number would either forbid legal yards or keep lying about the illegal ones.
dna.still_note:
WHAT SHOULD BITE AND WHAT SHOULD NOT, said in advance so a thin number is read correctly.

CONSTANT AT EVERY VALUE OF BOTH AXES, by construction: the apron, the four pads, the four kerb sets, the four lettered name tabs, and all thirty-two slot positions. Those are the control. A slot with no unit in it is drawn as an outline rather than left blank, which is why a bay that empties still reads as a bay — and it is also why `policy` cannot cheat by changing the footprint.

CONSTANT AT EVERY VALUE OF `circuit`: everything in the four bays. The whole circuit axis lives in the aisles and on the apron margin. `policy` should be the larger of the two numbers and is predicted at 26.68% against 18.29%.

TWO BAYS THAT SHOULD LOOK ALIKE, AND IT IS NOT A FAULT: `service` and `works` share their whole body — the same skid, the same shell, the same cover panel and the same lit lamp are drawn for both, and `works` adds apparatus on top. That is the one containment in the family (see dna.note) built as one, and the two bays are deliberately adjacent on the quad so a visitor can put them side by side. Do not 'fix' it by darkening the service unit.

NO TEXT NAMES AN AXIS VALUE OF THIS ARTIFACT. The rendered words in the yard are SERVICE, WORKS, STORE, SCRAP on the four name tabs, plus WORKS on a placard and SEALED and SCRAP on the units — all of them the exhibited family vocabulary, all of them present and identical in all sixteen frames. Not one pixel of any tile is a rendered word naming `policy` or `circuit`. Every one is a HangarKit.stencil or brand_patch quad, which is a real MeshInstance3D and enters the capture AABB; there is no Label3D anywhere in the file, so LabelFramer has nothing to bolt a panel behind.

IF IT COMES BACK FAINT, check three things before the design.
(1) Was --max at least 16? At the gallery default of 9 a 4x4 declaration renders 4x2 and `circuit` is measured on [loop, bays] alone — which is a large number rather than a faint one, but it would be a verdict about two values published as a verdict about four.
(2) Was the sweep run --staged? A 6.86 m yard is over the 6 m staging cut-off so it should not be plinthed, but if it were, the pair AABB would grow and every mark would shrink.
(3) Is the standpoint doing the work? This is a PLAN-VIEW artifact — four bays and a circuit between them — seen from 15 degrees above the ground. The routes are the marks most at risk from that, which is why they stand up rather than lie down. Per the standing gate an INERT verdict on this token is not reportable until tools/probe_anamorphic.py has been run on it; a probe from directly overhead should separate the circuit values far more than the canonical camera does, and if it does, the verdict is ANAMORPHIC and not INERT.
declines: `upkeep` AS THIS ARTIFACT'S AXIS. Refused for the reason slack_yard refused `slack`, and stated here so nobody reopens it. All seven family members use the word to stand in ONE condition and forgo the other three, so an axis over it would have four values each of which demolishes three quarters of this exhibit. Decided from the members' CODE: the four values are MIXED — works nests on service in 5 of 5 scripts, but store ADDS a covering while scrap SUBTRACTS material, and station_crates returns early on both rather than dressing the legacy stack — so no value contains all the others. That is the PARALLEL case, which is exactly the condition under which showing them all at once is NOT merely the top value, and is therefore the condition under which the retention_corridor move is available. The yard takes it: it stands all four, letters the word on a tab at each bay, and reads the word out of the family's own const rather than retyping it.

A `condition` OR `state` AXIS UNDER ANOTHER NAME. Considered and cut in one line: it is `upkeep` with the serial numbers filed off, and taking a word's answers without its word is the same dishonesty as taking a word without its answers (folding_past's ruling, inverted).

THE LAYOUT AS AN AXIS — rank / ring / pair / heap, i.e. how the four bays are arranged relative to each other. It is a real question and it makes a loud picture, and it was cut for a measurable reason: a rank of four bays is 6.5 x 1.3 m of subject and a ring is 5.6 x 5.6, so the UNION box would have been 8.8 x 5.6 and every mark in every frame would have shrunk by about 35% to accommodate two arrangements that are never in the same picture. `circuit` asks a better version of the same question — not where the conditions sit, but what joins them — and it does it at a fixed footprint.

ANY ANIMATION, RATE, DURATION OR DECAY. A yard has obvious time-domain axes — a throughput, a turnaround time, a queue building up — and every one of them is invisible to a still PNG. info_board shipped five duration exports and produced six identical tiles. The chain here is solved to its STATIONARY distribution precisely so that what is drawn is a standing fact about the yard rather than a moment in a process; there is no _process, no _physics_process, no Timer and no Tween anywhere in the file.

A FRAME-RELATIVE GAUGE. Every mark is 1:1 in metres against a ceiling fixed across the whole sweep: a dwell column of height h means pi = h / 1.20, a flow post of height h means flow = h / 4.00, in all sixteen frames. A 0.600 m column in the hoard frame and a 0.166 m column in the repair frame are the same instrument reading two numbers. Both gauges carry a datum collar at a fixed height (0.30 m on a column, 0.40 m on a post) so the ceiling is legible in the picture and not only in this file. sorting_hall normalised each frame to its own busiest row and its gauge then said nothing about the quantity it existed to show.

A PROXY FOR THE FLOW. The post measures pi[from] * P[from][to] — the fraction of the whole fleet that traverses that leg per period — and nothing else. Every one of the six legs is a single transition of the same chain, so no leg can silently report zero for a reason other than 'nothing goes this way': at hoard the `cond` and `repl` posts are 0.017 m tall, which is a true statement about a yard that condemns almost nothing, and the base plate and datum collar are still drawn under them so the leg is never unmarked. sorting_hall counted cells whose value changed as a proxy for work and reported that merge sort is free on sorted input.

ENGINEERING THE RATES TO HIT A TARGET ALLOCATION. It would have taken ten minutes to pick the four pictures and back out rates that produce them. The rates were chosen from each policy's meaning instead and the allocations are whatever they imply; the only constraint imposed from outside was that all four bays stay occupied, which is the artifact's thesis and not a cosmetic preference, and it cost two discarded rate sets rather than a fudged number.

PADDING THE CLOSEST PAIR. `bays` <-> `line` is predicted at 3.55-3.94% focus, which clears the critic's 3% INERT bar and sits under its 6% twin bar, and it was left there. It is thin because adding three arrows to a yard already holding sixteen dressed units is a small addition, and because ground marks foreshorten by sin(15 deg) at this camera. What WAS done is not padding but LAW 4: the naive arrows were given standing gate posts and chevron plates rather than being left as paint, which took the pair from 1.77% to 3.55% without changing a single route. Widening the lanes further would have made the yard's own naive-reading straw man louder than the circuit it is wrong about.
